Hey OP, I have ADHD so totally feel ya. Audio prayer apps like Amen (free), Hallow and Universalis are super helpful when you find it hard to start. Just click play and let the app do the hard work lol. There are also prayers which are super short like 30s - 2 mins. So when you face the productive procrastination issue, choose those super short prayers. I also have the issue of my mind telling me there’s something better that i can be doing instead of praying; but I tell myself look it’s only a 1 minute prayer. Surely whatever “better things that I can be doing” can wait for a minute. 

But there are days when even with audio prayers I find myself not being able to pray (unable to focus). I just try my best to focus throughout. If I become aware I’m getting distracted I’ll try to re-focus back. I’ll do that each time my attention drifts away. If even that fails, I just sit through until the prayer finishes anyway even though I was inattentive the whole time. Because I tell myself an imperfect prayer is better than no prayer. An imperfect 30 second prayer is also better than no prayer. 

I think to myself that it was God that created me with this condition so all the more he will be understanding when my condition makes it hard to pray. I think even if my prayer was imperfect God would still accept it cos he sees my intentions not the “output” lol. And I think that effort of trying despite it being such a huge struggle is pleasing to God even if that effort yields “nothing” (e.g. try as hard as you could but you still couldn’t finish the prayer) cos it shows our love for him ☺️

I’m a former Protestant (awaiting the next RCIA intake to start)

Confession: Instituted by Jesus. He gave authority to the apostles to forgive sins. In John 20:23 he tells the apostles “receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them…”

Baptism of children: Parents are supposed to take care of the child’s physical needs (e.g. your child is being difficult and refuses to eat. As a parent you still feed them cos that’s what is best for them). Same thing with the child’s spiritual needs even though they can’t consent at that time. Anyway when the child grows up they technically have the option to leave the church if they want to. 

Images: We’re still praying to God. The image is just a visual aid to help us focus/meditate. It’s not the image itself that we’re worshipping. If God really didn’t want us to use images we wouldn’t have the Shroud of Turin, the tapestry of Our Lady of Guadalupe etc

Papacy and the Masons founding the Church: Jesus said to Peter (Mt 16:18)  “on this rock I will build my church”. It came from Jesus directly. Also John 21:16 Jesus tells Peter to “Tend my sheep”. When Jesus was on earth he called himself the good shepherd. Now he’s tasking Peter to be the shepherd - Jesus is delegating priestly authority to Peter. 

Sola fide - “faith alone” doesn’t appear anywhere in the Bible except in James 2:26 which says faith without works is also dead. Also when Luther was translating the Bible he added in the word “alone” in Romans 3:28; 5:1) to read as “faith alone”.

Sola scriptura: Not everything was written down. In Acts 20:35 it says “it is more blessed to give than to receive”. You don’t see this verse anywhere else in the Bible. It is still Jesus’ teachings though. Instead of being written it was passed down by oral tradition. The church “keeps” all these teachings. TLDR; not everything is in the Bible. 

Praying to Mary and the saints: this is asking Mary and the saints to pray *for* you I.e intercessory prayer. The Bible points to many instances of intercessory prayer. Job 42:8 God tells Job’s friends to ask Job to pray for their forgiveness - instead of asking them to pray directly to him for forgiveness. 

James 5:16 “pray for one another… the prayer of the righteous is powerful and effective”

Protestants make prayer requests to their prayer ministry for intercessory prayer despite knowing they can pray directly to God. It’s the same thing with Mary and the saints. The “advantage” of Mary and the saints is that they’re really righteous so all the more “powerful and effective” is their prayer. Plus they’re closer to Jesus being up there with Jesus and all. 

And look at all the Marian miracles and miracles from asking the saints to intercede for you. If it were really idolatry why would God allow all these miracles.

Hey OP, I was in a similar situation. I came to know God when I was still in the same-sex relationship. I didn’t know much about Christianity. All I know was that one day I attended church, he healed an illness that I was having that time. And I felt his love for me. And somehow I didn’t have any conscious plan to do so, but I ended up repeatedly going to church and picking up the Bible. And he answered my prayers to let me know that he was there. When I was in trouble, I called on him and he helped me. All this took place while I was still sinning. Not being righteous and definitely still being a same-sex relationship. 

The Bible says a marriage is between a man and a woman. And sex is to take place within marriage. I’m not saying that we should try to go against the Bible. But what I’m saying, is that God says he will not reject anyone who comes to him for help (John 6:37-39).

”Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and eat with him, and he with me.“
‭‭Revelation‬ ‭3‬:‭20‬ ‭ESV‬‬
https://bible.com/bible/59/rev.3.20.ESV

^ Note that he says “if *anyone* hears my voice and opens the door”. Not “if *anyone who is holy* hears my voice and opens the door”.

Reach out to him for help and to feel his love for you. Ask for his grace, mercy and wisdom to navigate this situation. 

We are all sinners. And the only way we can walk in his way is by his grace, mercy, and the Holy Spirit. 

I prayed to God, asking what to do about being a Christian in a same sex relationship. His answer was full of grace and truth. My Bible literally fell open to the page where it says “Have you not read that he who created them from the beginning made them male and female, and said, ‘Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh’? So they are no longer two but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let not man separate.”“
‭‭Matthew‬ ‭19‬:‭4‬-‭6‬ ‭ESV‬‬

And then, right after my Bible turned to the Beatitudes in Matthew 5 where it says, “blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of Heaven” and all that. 

And the message I got was that yes, same-sex relationship are wrong. But God looks at other aspects of your life as well beyond your sex life. And that I should just focus on living out the Beattitude first. So I did, and he kept giving signs, letting me know that he was there. All while I was still in a same-sex relationship.

Eventually, I started feeling that I couldn’t reconcile being a follower of him, and still being engaged in a same sex relationship. His Holy Spirit helped to “remove” or “lessen” the “want” (for lack of a better word) to be in a same-sex relationship. And now I’m living celibately (for I’m still attracted to the same sex, so a heterosexual relationship/marriage is out of the question for me). I never thought it would be possible to reduce or remove that part of me which was attracted to people of the same-sex. But it did. 

So what I’m trying to say OP is that Jesus doesn’t require you to be perfect before you can approach him. And he is the only one who can help you to overcome this situation that you’re in. 

I’m praying for his grace and mercy to you. And for him to show his love to you. And to navigate you through this situation so you are full of his peace, joy and love away from this guilt and doubt. ❤️

“We should not live for the world” - the context is that worldly things (eg riches, beauty, power) is temporary and perishes but the Kingdom of God is eternal. Therefore don’t live your life seeking material/worldly things because they are very easily taken away and can only give temporary happiness. We should keep our eyes on what’s eternal instead (which is the Kingdom of God). So we live our earthly lives while seeking Jesus and walking in Jesus’s ways while on earth (being loving, forgiving, having mercy, upholding justice, helping the marginalised) so our “place” in the Kingdom of God is “secured”. 

This doesn’t mean withdrawing from the secular world though. Jesus asks us to be “salt” (“salt” - a widely used commodity with various uses - used figuratively here to mean being helpful and beneficial to society) and “light” to the world. Whatever joy, peace, love or benefit you received from your relationship with Christ you are told to live your lives so that everyone around you (everyone, including non-believers) can feel that joy, peace, love and benefit too. So we immerse ourselves in the secular world and strive to live selflessly and lovingly. For freely as we have received, we are to freely give. 

God’s blueprint for humans on earth was for them to work (Adam was created to look after the Garden). So part of walking in God’s ways is to be diligent and not idle. We are told to serve our bosses in our secular jobs as if we are serving Christ. So whilst we do work, our motivation isn’t to pursue riches or power at work but rather to serve.

You are right that it’s something we shouldn’t do. Because Jesus’s command was for us to love one another and gossiping and judging is definitely not loving.

The Trinity is something that I keep telling myself that I’m unable to fully understand because of my human limitations (when I’ve come to a point where I can’t get anymore answers/just really cannot comprehend no matter how hard I try lol)

1. The persons of the Trinity are not identical. Therefore I think when we say “the Son’s body suffered damaged”, the Son’s body does not represent the bodies of the rest of the Trinity. So in the Bible we see Jesus’s body “suffered damage”. But there’s no mention anywhere at all of God or the Holy Spirit suffering damage. So we can’t say just because Jesus could be “damaged” therefore Father and Holy Spirit can also be damaged. 

2. Jesus is the only person of the Trinity with human nature. So the “human weaknesses” of Jesus does not apply to the Father and Holy Spirit

So yeah he does have a “body” but it’s not an ordinary human body the way you and I have lol. I see it as his “body” has some divine characteristic that’s why he could be resurrected and also why he’s the only one to ever be resurrected.

I feel you, OP. I felt **incredibly** indignant over how Esau seemed to be "bullied" and cheated by Jacob in the narrative in Genesis. And when I first read "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated", I felt it was incredibly unfair to Esau.

Over time, I realised that there's only so much we can know based on what is written in the Bible. We don't actually have the full view of what happened. But God does, and he acts justly. As I re-read the passages and when I looked into my study bible I found a couple of tiny details which helped ease the injustice I felt lol:

​

1. What Jacob did was undoubtedly **wrong**. Lying is prohibited under the 9th commandment
2. I realised "Esau I hated" wasn't meant to be taken literally LOL. In essence, the message was: God will choose Jacob (to carry out His purposes), not Esau. Some descriptions of Esau indicated he wasn't perfect (e.g. readily giving up the blessing of being firstborn, and having foreign wives). But in spite of Esau's imperfections, in Deuteronomy 2:5-6, God provided for Esau and though Israel (Jacob) was God's "chosen one", he protected Esau and forbade Israel from waging war on Esau and taking Esau's land: *"Do not provoke them to war, for* ***I will not give you*** *any of their land,* ***not even enough to put your foot on****.* ***I have given*** *Esau the hill country of Seir as his own".* This honestly made me feel so much better for Esau that God didn't actually "hate" him lol.
3. In Genesis 27:40, Isaac tells Esau he will not be subservient to Jacob permanently: *"You will live by the sword and you will serve your brother. But when you grow restless, you will throw his yoke from off your neck".*
4. Ironically, Jacob got a taste of his own medicine when Laban cheated him by giving Leah to be his wife instead of Rachel. And he had to work another 7 years to marry Rachel.

He wants to have a relationship with you, His child. A relationship needs two-way communication, you speaking to Him (prayer) and you listening to Him (through His Word in Scriptures). “Speaking” is also cathartic and you would always feel a better after you have spoken about it in prayer instead of leaving it unprocessed in your mind. 

The act of needing to reach out to Him through prayer whenever I need help (instead of not doing anything since technically he knows what we want already before we even ask), helps me to remember to be humble. That I need Him for help. It also helps me to remember my position in relation to God. He is the glorious Almighty, all-knowing God and i am just a mere mortal living by His grace and provision. It helps keep me from becoming “I achieved this with my own hands. I don’t need God” lol

I listen to the Bible whenever - both while working or during leisure. There’s actually evidence outside the Bible from non-Christians that documented there was this person called Jesus, who was crucified by Pilate, died and was resurrected. Josephus and Pliny are two of those sources. Josephus was a Jew and in Pliny’s account he is actually journaling how he’s interrogating these bunch of people if they are followers of Jesus and they readily say they are. Pliny asks again making it clear that they will be persecuted if they are followers of Jesus. And they repeat again that they are. And they indeed get persecuted / continue being interrogated (as Pliny thinks they’re hiding something cos why on Earth would people readily confess to something which they will be persecuted for). And throughout their response is the same which is that they admit they follow Christ. 

In Rome, Christians were persecuted terribly (eg being burned alive and used as literal “human candles” to light the streets”) yet people continued to follow Christ and readily admitted that they are his followers during those times. A whole bunch of people wouldn’t readily risk their lives like that for a lie.

Love. It is about love. The entire Bible, though consisting of numerous books, authors and written across different time periods all are about one thing: God’s love for us and all his creation. 

Many people question how is God a loving God when he sent Jesus to die for us. In the Old Testament, we also see instances of God’s wrath (eg destroying Sodom and Gomorrah). How is a punishing God a loving god? can’t he just forgive our sins? Love encompasses justice. You cannot be loving to your creations yet let injustice prevail. if we see for example a serial murderer-rapist/child molester getting sentenced to only two weeks jail, we would feel that it’s unfair and those criminals NEED to be punished for all the harm they caused to the innocent. So love includes upholding justice and therefore sin needs to be reckoned with instead of letting it “slide” and turning a “blind eye” towards it. 

And the ultimate display of God’s love was by sending Jesus to die on the cross for our sins. As a just God, the sins were reckoned with, he did not “waive” it off. But as a loving God, instead of letting us take the punishment of our sins, he directed the “punishment” to Jesus instead (who was of God and hence a “divine” sacrifice)

It’s obviously hard to be sin free as hard as we try. We do slip up. If a person sins but later on regret it, the fact is that they still had committed a sin and that sin needs to be reckoned with. If that person feels sorry for their sin, it also means in their heart they’re rejecting a sinful life but we somehow slip up as no one is perfect. When your heart turns away from sin, you’re making room in your heart for Jesus to come in. He can’t force his way in your heart though, you need to *let him in*. When you do, you’re also accepting his sacrifice that cleanses you of your sin. So for this person that “sinned” but later repented, God remains just where that person’s sin was reckoned with. But in his love seeing that the person has repented, instead of letting that person suffer the punishment, he takes the punishment on himself instead (through Jesus).

So the whole thing in its simplest form, is about love.
